correctness.rationale: PASS: Each nonalgebraic type is a consistent ideal/filter pair. The one-sided patterns count 2J_n-1. Nonempty two-sided patterns are supported precisely by singletons (7n), adjacent pairs (3n), distance-two pairs (n), and consecutive triples (n), hence 12n for all n>=5. Counting ideals via cyclic zero-triples gives the displayed de Bruijn transfer matrix with characteristic polynomial lambda(lambda-1)(lambda^2-2lambda-1), so J_n=1+(1+sqrt2)^n+(1-sqrt2)^n and t_n=2J_n-1+12n. Direct ternary enumeration n=5,6,7 and independent subset/word checks n=5..14 passed; these finite tests do not replace the complete proof.

value.rationale: PASS: The named finite parameter family is a canonical cyclic three-uniform hypergraph incidence poset (regular, arbitrary length), and exact pointwise-stabilizer type growth is natural in a generally #P-complete setting. The result simultaneously gives a closed-form infinite count and the sharp structural fact that exactly 12n types lie on both sides of the parameter poset while the total grows with base 1+sqrt2. That linear/exponential separation is a meaningful non-obvious type-spectrum invariant, not just a recomputation of individual small tables.
